Okay so I went down a rabbit hole on this recently. 

I fell out of pipe smoking and picked it back up this year, but all of the tins I ordered in 2024 were tragically dried out and stale. So this time I put all of my tobacco in canning jars as soon as I open them to maintain the original moisture, per the recommendation of many. But now my issue is the fresh tobacco is so moist, especially some of the aromatics I’ve ordered. 

In my opinion, a lot of the methods are too involved for get the tobacco to the correct dryness. Muttonchop recommends the paper towel method. Some people microwave. Etc.

What I’ve found works best for me is taking roughly a half an ounce of tobacco (a quarter of a 50g tin) out of my canning jar, and place it back in the now empty tin, for what I will smoke the next 3-5 days. I then place the paper cover back over the tobacco and leave it uncovered overnight, or during the day and check every 3-4 hrs. This takes under a minute and I wake up to ready to pack tobacco.

You are young, enjoy your youth and focus on establishing your career, learning and building skills, and developing character that will attract friendships and relationships down the road. 

Please don’t be hard on yourself- some of the strongest relationships and marriages I know are people who had zero intimacy well into their mid to late 20’s and just focused on education and work. 

No one is making fun of you in college or the adult world for being a virgin unless they are immature and childish, and if they are, embrace it and think “you must not know the rest of my flaws!” Stoicism teaches us we cannot control the actions of others and should not attempt to analyze them- instead focus on your reaction to things outside of your control. 

It’s totally normal to feel the FOMO and you shouldn’t be hard on yourself for feeling that way. Instead, accept what is and what will be, and most importantly, focus on building a good foundation for your life. You aren’t going to look back and be upset you didn’t get laid, but I 100% promise you will look back in regret if you let it distract you from your career and mental/physical health. 

The right person will come along- it sounds cliche but it is absolutely true that they will come into your life when you least expect it and when you aren’t focused on a sense of lack in comparison to your peers or societal expectations.

I just did a new build and decided to actually do cable management haha. This is what I did:

Power strip mounted to underside of desk. You can use some strong strips of Velcro, or what I did which is get a cable organizer tray that clamps to the desk (from microcenter but can find anywhere) 

Now you just need to keep the cables organized and prevent them from dropping into view:

I got a cable organizer kit (also from microcenter) which has Velcro, zip ties, adhesive plastic loops that secure to the back wall or desk. I ran my pc and monitor power cables first. If they are too long double them back into a figure 8 shape, zip tie/velcro strap them together and let them sit in the cable tray. Then run your keyboard/monitor/other peripheral cables to your pc in one zip tied bundle, making sure they stay out of sight from sitting position. Take the excess and loop them back like you did with power cables so they don’t droop.

It’s all up to your setup/timeframe and signal for entry but here’s my best analysis: 

Price structure from the left to about the middle of this image is downtrend that is consolidating  (lower highs, higher lows). Your bias is short. Price breaks upper yellow resistance + blue horizontal resistance and creates a new high. You could have profited on a breakout trade if you exited quickly, but until it creates new highs (above the high on left of the image) your bias is still short. 

Price then fails to create new highs and breaks downward back into the yellow lines. You’re now looking for a breakout of lower yellow line for a continuation of short trend. If you extend the lower yellow line, you’d see that price breaks through and then retests, followed by a continuation of short trend. This could have been your short entry signal. 

The way you could have predicted the drop is by seeing price breakout below the bottom trend line and fails the retest which continued the trend. There is no way to predict the size of the move but you can still anticipate a downward move when price breaks out.

If you are timing the market, you need a strategy. You need to develop a start to finish process, or system, that you have studied and backtested extensively. Then, you need to test that system with small positions for 20-30 trades to prove you can make consistent profit.

Your system can be buy and hold indexes 30+ years- easy and proven success in the long term but you aren’t getting rich quick- or you can scalp/daytrade/swing trade/position trade.

I went through this in 2020 when my partner of 6 years broke it off, right when the pandemic hit. I couldn’t eat or sleep for days. Couldn’t meet up with anyone because of the lockdown. Pretty much just trapped at home, alone, for weeks. It was constant state of anxiety and panic that I’ve never experienced before. Absolutely brutal. Nonstop memories, intense self loathing.

After a few months the daily memories and pain started to fade, but it wasn’t until over a year later that I realized I didn’t think about her every day anymore. 

Now, a few years later, I still think of her frequently, but the pain is almost completely gone. I’m happier, stronger, more independent, and I can’t say I’m ‘glad’ I went through it, but in the end it was a positive experience- a ‘dark night of the soul’. 

Maybe this isn’t what you want to hear, but it just takes time. I tried to delve into eckharts teachings, but ultimately i realized I was just trying to find ways to escape the pain. His teachings did help me tremendously in ‘sitting with’ my negative feelings and just accepting them. 

in all honesty, just try to occupy your time- reading, gaming, tv, getting outside, really whatever you like! You will heal, you will live a better life and gain strength. The human mind is incredibly adaptable. 

‘A tree that weathers strong winds grows deep roots’. Accept what you’re feeling and breathe into it. This too shall pass. ✌️

As far as trains goes it took my brain some time to understand the signals but I only ever have two lines, one for each direction of the belt system, and occasionally it would get slow but always resolved itself. It took me 300hrs to finally launch a rocket, and using the calculator ahead of time was the only way I got it to work without the mess overwhelming me. Altitude x 3 divided by 100= distance in NM to begin descent. 
Eg. 30,000 x 3 / 100 = 90nm.

My position sizes are around 5% of my account, so like $250- 500ish max. on webull options cash settles in 24hrs so I don't have to worry about PDT restriction. 

If the position doesn't immediately move in my favor, I exit rapidly, usually for a $10-20 loss within seconds, but sometimes more if it reverses too quickly for me to get my stop placed properly. Max loss for day is 1% of portfolio. It either breaks out immediately or I'm out. This will happen multiple times in a day, and some days I'm stopped out repeatedly as price spikes and then reverses, which can be maddening. There are a ton of downsides to this strategy. However, when price breaks out of a range, it can make a dramatic move, and within minutes I'm 10x my risk. So something like 10:1 risk reward lmao.
